newsitem.title: UK: Morrison, United Utilities win PFI deal.
newsitem.headline: Morrison, United Utilities win PFI deal.

text.p: The Catchment consortium, comprising Britain's Morrison Construction Plc, United Utilities and Bechtel of the U.S. have been given the go-ahead for a privately financed sewerage project at Inverness and Fort William in Scotland, the group said on Monday.

North of Scotland Water Authority signed the deal, clearing the way for construction to begin. Morrison and Bechtel will be reponsible for the building work which is expected to cost 45 million stg, with United Utilities responsible for operating the system over the 25-year contract term.
The total value of the deal has not been revealed.
The three companies are equal partners in the private finance initiative (PFI) project.
PFI is a flagship government policy set up to suck private sector capital into public infrastructure projects, allowing companies to finance, build and operate.
Michael Martin, managing director of Morrison's infrastructure development division, said on behalf of the consortium that it was a "pioneering project".
